items.title: What AI tells small-business borrowers: loan information, pricing and fair lending
items.summary: How chatbots, marketplaces, accounting platforms and lenders' own assistants change what small-business owners can learn about loan options, prices and eligibility, and why fair-lending and disclosure rules reach only some of them. Usage figures and product claims are mostly self-reported, and the public data that could measure outcomes is being cut back.

items.title: AI in SBA lending: where it is used, what the rules say, and the risks
items.summary: Where lenders, vendors and the SBA itself use AI across the 7(a) and 504 process, from intake to servicing, and how SOP 50 10 8.1, the LSP rules and the guaranty already constrain it. The public deployments cluster in loans of $350,000 or less, and every performance figure is the lender's or vendor's own.

items.title: TD Credit Assist and the rise of AI copilots for credit analysts
items.summary: What TD Bank U.S. has disclosed about Credit Assist, its October 2026 multi-agent tool that drafts commercial credit memos, how it compares with DBS and vendor copilots, and the governance banks put around such tools. Every performance figure is TD's own, from pre-launch testing, and US model risk guidance leaves these tools out of scope.

items.title: AI-first banks in small-business lending: Live Oak, Huntington and Casca
items.summary: What Live Oak, Huntington and other US banks have publicly launched to put AI into small-business and SBA lending, and what they report. The Huntington–Casca link is confirmed but unexplained in public, Live Oak's Casca rollout is still a pilot, and no bank has yet published a measured result.

items.title: Lumos and alternative credit scoring for small business
items.summary: What Lumos (Lumos Data) is, how its expected-loss score is built and what it does not disclose, set against bureau scores, cash-flow scoring and FICO SBSS, which the SBA stopped using for 7(a) Small Loans in March 2026. Independent studies show real but modest gains from alternative data, concentrated in thin-file borrowers.

items.title: OCR spreading tools vs LLMs for financial statement extraction
items.summary: Compares dedicated auto-spreading tools with general LLM extraction on accuracy, failure modes, auditability, cost and validation, using public benchmarks, vendor materials and US guidance. The best LLMs now read financial pages as well as good OCR, but their errors are silent, so the controls around the extractor matter more than the engine.
